What Dr. Annie Does for TIB HIND Patients

Dr. Annie's role is to bring clinical context into the first stage of medical-travel planning. She helps the coordination team understand the file, recognise important gaps and prepare the right questions before a case is discussed as a travel or cost enquiry.

01

Read the available records

She reviews the reports shared for the case, including the diagnosis, imaging summaries, laboratory results, treatment history and current concerns.

02

Identify missing information

If the file is incomplete, the review can highlight which report, scan, pathology material or clinical detail may be needed before a hospital can respond meaningfully.

03

Clarify the specialist pathway

The purpose is to help identify the type of specialist or multidisciplinary team that should assess the patient, not to select a doctor from a title alone.

04

Review the proposed direction

When a hospital opinion is received, the medical-review role helps the coordination team understand the terminology, questions and areas that need clarification.

05

Support a better patient discussion

The patient receives practical questions to ask the treating team about alternatives, risks, investigations, recovery, follow-up and the basis of the estimate.

06

Flag urgent concerns

If the records suggest a time-sensitive issue, the patient is advised to seek immediate local medical assessment rather than wait for travel coordination.

Scope of this review: this is not an emergency service, a final diagnosis, a prescription or a guarantee that treatment in India is appropriate. The hospital and treating consultant remain responsible for examination, consent, clinical decisions and care.

Professional background

About Dr. Annie Varughese

Dr. Annie T. Varughese is a US-based cardiologist whose published professional background includes cardiovascular disease, interventional cardiology and preventive heart care. TIB HIND works with her as a medical review partner so the first conversation begins with the patient's records and clinical questions, not only a requested procedure or price.

Her primary professional biography describes a medical degree from the Medical College of Georgia, internal-medicine training and a cardiovascular-disease fellowship at the University of Texas Medical School at Houston, followed by further interventional-cardiology training at the Texas Heart Institute and Baylor College of Medicine.

The US National Provider Identifier Registry lists Annie T. Varughese, MD, under NPI 1639112170. Registry information confirms professional identity and taxonomy; it does not by itself establish suitability for a particular patient or procedure.

FAQs
Before sending records

Questions About Dr. Annie's Review Role

Does Dr. Annie treat every TIB HIND patient?

No. Her TIB HIND role is medical review and clinical-context support. Diagnosis, prescribing, procedures and hospital treatment remain the responsibility of the doctor and hospital formally accepting the patient.

Is a record review the same as a medical consultation?

No. A record review can help organise information and identify useful questions, but it does not replace an examination, a formal doctor-patient consultation or emergency assessment.

Which records are useful for review?

The most useful file usually includes a short medical summary, recent consultation notes, laboratory reports, imaging reports, pathology reports where relevant, current medicines and details of previous treatment. Requirements vary by condition.

Can Dr. Annie guarantee that a hospital will accept a case?

No. Each hospital and treating specialist decides whether it can accept the case after reviewing the records, available expertise, capacity and the patient's clinical circumstances.

Can patients request a cardiology-focused review?

Yes. Patients considering cardiac evaluation or treatment can ask TIB HIND to organise an initial record review and identify suitable next questions. A formal opinion or treatment plan must come from the responsible treating cardiologist or hospital.

Does TIB HIND provide emergency medical advice?

No. Anyone with chest pain, severe breathlessness, fainting, stroke symptoms, heavy bleeding or sudden deterioration should contact local emergency services immediately.
